member.name: T:Sim.Telemetry.AngleTrace
member.summary: Turns a wrapped angular sample series (compass bearings, headings, signed wind angles) into a continuous one by following the short way round the circle at each step — so the 0↔period seam doesn't render as a full-height vertical jump and a plot can auto-centre on wherever the data sits. Pure so the seam logic is unit-tested independent of Godot. period is one full turn in the samples' own unit (2π for radians, 360 for degrees).

member.name: M:Sim.Telemetry.AngleTrace.Unwrap(System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Single},System.Single)
member.summary: Unwrap in place-order: each output tracks the previous by the shortest angular step, so a 359°→2° pair becomes 359°→362° (a +3° move). Absolute level is anchored to the first sample; callers that show axis labels should re-wrap for display.

member.name: M:Sim.Telemetry.AngleTrace.WrapSym(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Fold an angular delta into (−period/2, +period/2] so it takes the short way round. A non-positive period passes the delta through unchanged (non-angular data).

member.name: T:Sim.Telemetry.AxisRange
member.summary:
A plot's vertical axis bounds for a data window [dataMin, dataMax], chosen so the zero line is meaningful:
All-non-negative data → baseline anchored at 0 (only the top is padded), so fluctuations read in proportion to the absolute value — a 6800–7000 µs frame time shows as a near-flat line high on the plot, not a full-height swing.
Signed data → symmetric about 0 (Min == -Max), so the zero line sits in the middle.
Pure so the branch logic (non-negative / signed / degenerate) is unit-tested independent of Godot.

member.name: T:Sim.Telemetry.FleetPerfChannels
member.summary: Per-frame CPU + render cost of the boats, so a host can see where a fleet spends its budget: the chased (detailed) boat's physics + AI vs the rest of the fleet vs all boats, and the render cost of the environment vs the chased boat vs every boat. All are per-frame sums (over the substeps). and carry the frame budget so their utilisation reads as a % of the frame — the numbers that tell you whether the fleet, not one boat, is the cost.
